mechanisms.behavior: A-14970-1 motor 14-7969/crank rotates the bookcase to hide or expose the Vault shot. Real microswitches 81/82 report open/closed; four optical impact channels 53–56 in the bookcase face register hits for GREED independently of rotation. Exact Gold host model cvpmMech uses solenoid 27, length 100, steps 90, reverse/nonlinear motion, closed 82 at 0–1 and open 81 at 89–90. Those are model units, not physical degrees/timing. Initialize from the actual bookcase pose; the native cyclic model and the host model use different counter phases. Startup/service motor search requires real feedback to follow movement. T.13 toggles motor and displays limits. A jam or missing limit must remain visible to the ROM; never force both limits active. Native taf_handleMech uses an alternative 200-tick cyclic model, not the physical construction.
mechanisms.label: Motorized rotating bookcase (Vault)

mechanisms.behavior: A-14711 in locations, A-17411 in 2-27 heading, motor 14-7966 and two opto limits on A-15285 with A-15310 interrupter. Coil 6/A-12158-1 magnet travels in the hand to pick up a ball from saucer 87, carry it over the box, then drop it into the return path. Exact Gold cvpmMech uses coil 25, length 175, steps 60, reverse/nonlinear, down 84 at 0–1 and up 85 at 59–60; these are host model units. T.12 motor test toggles motor and displays both limits; Operation Test cycles pickup/drop with a ball. Initialize the hand and its two limits from its actual pose, with the magnet off; a down resting pose is usual but is not guaranteed after interruption. Keep the two limits mutually exclusive and report jams/missed pickup through actual sensor/ball state rather than teleporting a successful ball.

The script lifts its stored ball with the Thing animation, releases it into the hand return lane, then switch 77/coil 7 return it to play.
